findings.evidence: Lines 110-116 (mulLeft) use `f.comp (ContinuousMap.mulLeft g)`; line 130 uses `⟨fun g ↦ f g⁻¹, _⟩`. `Homeomorph.inv` exists (mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean:320).
findings.fix: State the argument via a bundled continuous inversion map so it parallels the translation lemmas, e.g. `haarAverage G (f.comp (Homeomorph.inv G : C(G, G)))`, keeping @[simp]; otherwise drop @[simp].
findings.issue: haarAverage_comp_inv is @[simp] but its argument is a raw `⟨fun g ↦ f g⁻¹, _⟩` (i.e. `ContinuousMap.mk` with a non-Miller-pattern body). Downstream inversion terms arise as `f.comp _` (`ContinuousMap.comp`), never as this literal `mk`, so the simp lemma will essentially never fire — unlike haarAverage_comp_mulLeft/mulRight which match on `.comp` and do fire.

findings.evidence: `ContinuousLinearMap` is a `ContinuousMapClass`, so `(L : C(V,W))` coerces via `toContinuousMap` (mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Defs.lean:64) and `ContinuousMap.comp` gives `fun g ↦ L (f g)`.
findings.fix: State it with the bundled coercion, e.g. `haarAverage G ((L : C(V, W)).comp f) = L (haarAverage G f)`, matching the `.comp` forms.
findings.issue: haarAverage_comp_comm takes the composed map as an anonymous `⟨fun g ↦ L (f g), _⟩`, an awkward interface a consumer cannot match against a naturally bundled map.

summary: Clean CLM surface with a complete characteristic API, but haarAverage_comp_inv is marked @[simp] while its LHS is an anonymous ContinuousMap.mk with a non-pattern lambda, so it cannot fire on naturally composed maps and is inconsistent with the translation lemmas. haarAverage_comp_comm shares the same awkward anonymous-argument interface.
